To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the localization of oskar RNA is determined by competition of two motors: kinesin- and myosin.

the localization of osk mRNA to the posterior pole of Drosophla oocyte is determined by the competition between kinesins and myosin, which is in turn determined by the density of cortical microtubules in the oocyte.
kinesin- and myosin-dependent motor activities determine the localization of the oskar mRNA, and that these activities are balanced to define the posterior pole of Drosophla oocytes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms that control the asymmetric distribution of proteins and RNAs in cells.
the mechanisms of RNA localization and the role of RNA localization in development.
the mechanisms of cytoskeletal motor-driven transport in cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
posterior localization is determined by the relative strength of kinesin- and myosin-mediated forces at different sites in the oocyte.
the posterior localization of oskar mRNA and the subsequent establishment of the posterior pole are determined by the competition between kinesins and myosins.
kinesin- 1 and myosim-V compete for osk/Staefun localization, and that the outcome of the competition is determined by microtubule and actin filament density.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the posterior cortex of Drosophia oocyte is determined by a combination of low microtubules density and high myosin-V activity.
the posterior localization of oskar mRNA in the D. melanogaster oocyte is determined by the competition between the microtubule-based motor kinesin-2 and actin-based motor myosin-V.
microtubule and actin motors compete to determine the position of the Drosophia posterior pole.
The main takeaway from our work is that
kinesin and myosin compete for the same cargo and that the outcome of this competition is determined by the density of microtubules at the cortex.
kinesin- and myosin-mediated transport can be antagonistic and that their competition determines the final distribution of cargo.
competition between motors is a powerful mechanism that determines the localization of a cargo in cells.
